exposure: Ex utero intrapartum delivery with tumor resection
cohort: Eight fetuses with suspected intrapericardial teratoma were seen at a single center from 2009 through 2015.
finding: Fetal intrapericardial teratoma can be successfully managed through timely intervention based on increasing tumor size and declining cardiac output to prevent hydrops, with in utero surgical resection being a possible and effective treatment.
mod_finding: One case was successfully treated at 31 weeks through ex utero intrapartum delivery with tumor resection while on placental support.
followup_time: At least until term for surviving cases (one case delivered at 37 weeks with excellent outcome).
gest_age: Gestational age at initial presentation ranged from 21-34 weeks (median 26 weeks).
